known_gaps: turning the customer's words into negotiation events (and dates into YYYY-MM-DD) is done by the dialogue model; offers, counters, dates, amounts, read-back, recording, notes and the close are code
callback window validity is decided by the dialogue model from code-computed window facts (not code)
identity flow (which question, re-asks, declines) follows the dialogue model with the bank's verification results

extra rule (stateful, stage opening): Ask for identity confirmation at most twice; a customer question answered first does not reset the count; close not_reached/unclear after the second unclear ask. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage identity): Identity refusals: explain once, then close not_verified/declined on the second refusal or the second 'what is this about' question. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
extra rule (stateful, stage identity): Track wrong identity answers across both questions; unreadable values and swapped day/month retries do not count. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Persuasion attempts counted per product: flat refusals/non-answers use one; early band 1 attempt, late band 2; do not repeat a refused offer; a customer-proposed date or amount is never a refusal; refusing the floor or the deadline counts as a flat refusal. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Offer the floor only once after 'too much' or a below-floor amount; then subsequent attempt 1 uses the floor. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage negotiate): Interpret 'next <weekday>' as that weekday in the following calendar week and 'this <weekday>' as the current week, relative to now. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage negotiate): A weekend/holiday date not after the deadline is moved to the next business day as an offer (needs customer acceptance). - left to the dialogue model's prompt
extra rule (stateful, stage global): A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first; transfer to general only if they insist. - left to the dialogue model's prompt
extra rule (stateful, stage global): Two statements of not wanting to talk close the call: no_promise/refused after verification, not_verified/declined before. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it; agreed but unrecorded promises are not recorded on a restructuring request. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (computational, stage closing): Without a recorded promise, close reason is that of the first product in get_account order whose note is not paid; paid if all noted paid. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

extra rule (stateful, stage negotiate): Hardship (illness, death in the family, job loss) comes before persuasion and restructuring: sympathy, no persuasion, offer support transfer; a date/amount the customer still names is recorded. - left to the dialogue model's prompt

unresolved conflict: Hardship in multi-product calls: chose 'Hardship applies to the call: no persuasion; offer support transfer; if declined, note every unpromised product hardship (unless already noted dispute/paid) and close per Brief B closing' (Brief B does not replace rule 32 per product; only disputes and already-paid claims are stated to continue the call.)

unresolved conflict: A transfer after a recorded promise when the request is for a human or support: chose "transferred with that transfer's reason" (Brief A says: 'If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as transferred with that transfer's reason'; the Brief B exception for rule 10 is consistent with this.)
checks: first security answer reaches verify_identity with the right field
no account or write call before verification
negotiation stage reached with account facts
every product's past-due amount stated in the debt statement, before any offer

promise date validity (past / after deadline / non-business day)

amount: full first, floor offer after 'too much' or a below-floor amount, accept floor..full
shared date clamped to each product's deadline
read-back of the whole package, confirmation bound to that package, writes only from the confirmed package
hardship: one code-owned sympathy+support offer, no persuasion afterwards, customer's own date/amount kept
notes per product (used), none after a transfer; close outcome from recorded/transfer/product results
goodbye -> notes -> exactly one close_call in the negotiation path
model: turning the customer's words into events and dates into YYYY-MM-DD (calendar table given)
identity question order, re-asks, declines (bank result routes to the account step)
opening confirmation and its re-ask count
third party, callback window validity and re-ask
transfer decision and queue (close mapping is code)
questions outside payment (robot/scam answers come from the policy)
